topics.title: Reflection of Light by Curved Mirrors
topics.subject: physics
topics.subStrand: Reflection of light at curved surfaces
outcomes: Understand reflection of light and the formation of images by curved mirrors (u)
Use ray diagrams to show how images are formed by curved mirrors and the nature of the images (s)

body.text: A concave mirror curves inward, like the inside of a spoon. A convex mirror curves outward, like the back of a spoon. Both reflect light, but they form images very differently from a flat (plane) mirror.

A concave mirror can focus parallel rays of light to a single point, called the focal point, at a distance called the focal length from the mirror. Depending on how far an object is from a concave mirror, it can form a magnified, real image (used in torches, satellite dishes, and shaving mirrors) or a different kind of image altogether.

A convex mirror always forms a smaller, upright image, and it gives a wider field of view than a flat mirror of the same size. This is why convex mirrors are used as vehicle wing mirrors and in shops, to see a wide area at a glance.
Use the PhET Geometric Optics: Basics simulation below (Mirror screen). Move an object in front of a concave or convex mirror and see how the image changes.
